newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies rally, bellies close sharply up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies rally, bellies close sharply up.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures rallied late with hogs ending mixed and pork bellies up sharply on mostly technical and some commercial support, traders said.
Hog futures ended 0.150 cent higher to 0.300 lower with April off 0.075 at 74.950 cents. Pork bellies surged to close 1.900 to 1.450 cent higher with March up 1.575 at 80.725.

Hog futures fell when profit taking and long liquidation touched off sell stops, but prices rallied back at the close after holding technical support. Much of the late action appeared technical, traders said.

Some pressure stemmed from the outlook for seasonally increasing hog marketings coupled with previous reports that some packers would be cutting kills or closing slaughter plants starting next week, they said.
"Seasonally, cash hog prices from February into April go down and you have April at a premium" to the index, said Dale Durchholz, market analyst with AgriVisor Services Inc.
The latest CME lean hog index was up $0.87 at $69.78 per cwt while April started the day at 75.025.
Rand Financials and E.D.&F. Man closing buy orders offset midday selling buy R.J. O'Brien, Refco and Rosenthal Collins. Cargill Investor Services bought April and sold July, pit sources said.
In hog options, Rand sold 80 and 82 July calls earlier. Locals bought 71 to 73 April puts on the break and then bought calls on the late rally, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures rallied late as fund buying on strong technicals and commercial support from plans to cut slaughter combined to touch off buy stops, traders said.
"We're looking ahead to (hog packing) plant closings" next week, one trader said.

Bellies started higher on carryover demand from Wednesday's sharp gains before profit taking and local selling took prices down to previous levels. Prices recovered late as the market remained technically very strong. Fund buying increased and added to commercial interest to take futures up sharply to new days highs with March up to its best level in one month, traders said.
E.D.&F. Man bought March and May with Cargill and Iowa Grain buyers in May. R.J. O'Brien sold May, pit sources said.
